latestPosts.caption:
Yesterday I attended the #TIME100 Summit in NYC 🏙️ 

Here are the main things I learned:

1. Everyone is ADDICTED to their phones... ppl literally cannot sit still and listen. At one point, every single person sitting around me was on their phones checking email/slack/socials instead of listening. I'm prolly one of the only people who does NOT have social/email/slack on my phone. Now I realize this is a superpower.

Also, I worry ppl are too obsessed with AI itself... I teach AI, so that you can build leverage and have more flexibility to enjoy what TRULY MATTERS to you.

2. Posting/streaming to socials gets my free AI education to a much bigger and more diverse audience compared to exclusive events. I view social media as the most efficient distribution engine for education; if it wasn't, I wouldn't use it.

3. For me, Richard Edelman stole the show with a strong thesis that businesses should be societal leaders, i.e. consistently demonstrating the values you want to see in the world instead of relegating this responsibility to the realm of "politics" only 🦁 when I noticed the lack of free high-quality AI education and the worsening AI literacy gap, I didn’t need anyone’s PERMISSION to do something about it. I embraced my vision - free education for all so that no one is left behind - as my personal responsibility. (Kierkegaard, much?)

4. Tougher AI topics like the widening class gap, widening literacy gap, culture of fear, job displacement, and lack of upskilling were only lightly touched on... the palatable answer was... "our plan is to upskill employees so we can still fire them but they can be hired SOMEWHERE ELSE"... lol ppl wonder why I don't care about teaching AI to big companies (answer: the gains DO NOT trickle down to you employees)

NOBODY acknowledged the massive overhiring when interest rates were low, leading to multiple rounds of layoffs. NOBODY talked about how the headline "we're firing ppl because of AI" is often because it's a much nicer spin than ..."we overhired when money was cheap and didn't hit revenue targets".

It was probably around two and a half years ago when I first questioned if any of this was possible.

I’m a very long way from where I need to be, but at least I’m a long way from where I was. And I will celebrate the W’s I took and the lessons I learned. 

What I’ve realized is that where I “need” to be doesn’t matter. It’s all relative and I will always want more.

My satisfaction just comes from climbing the mountain. Reaching the top is just another accolade. Then onto the next mountain.

And my comfortability of no longer needing to reach a certain level of stasis has given me peace. 

I had it wrong for so long: I figured that if I put my head down and optimized every aspect of my life, routine, time management, and so on… 

If I could be 100% efficient, and sheer force my way until I get what I want: I would only then have the freedom to live like I deserved it.

I obviously never reached that. I thought that “balance” would destroy my ability to outperform people. And there are two factors that transformed my perspective on this: People and experiences. 

This past year I have had a variety of incredible people introduced to my life. 

“Incredible” can’t even describe the potency of love I have for the people around me. 

And travelling across the planet opened my eyes. A bunch of successful entrepreneurs on a mission in Africa. 

Easily some of the coolest people I’ve ever met. 

This really made me shift my focus from increasing output to increasing leverage. This is how I can reintroduce balance into my life, not by locking in harder.  

2025 was all about ‘stuff’. 2026 my sights are set on doing cool shit, exploring the planet, and most importantly… 

Doing it with the people I value more than anything else. 

I feel so blessed. What did I ever do to deserve this. 

Most used phrase on the trip: “Bro we’re literally in Africa right now”
Gotta try this. #ai #aiautomation
